title: Martingality in EFM Signature Volatility Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.35022v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We establish a martingality criterion for the Exponentially Fading Memory (EFM) signature volatility model, extending the recent result of Abi Jaber, Gassiat, and Sotnikov (2026). In the proposed framework, the volatility process is given by a linear functional of the EFM signature of a time-augmented Brownian motion, which yields a globally well-behaved, fully non-Markovian volatility model admitting a stationary distribution. The stationary EFM signature volatility model is also covered by allowing for a random initial value of the signature. Moreover, the volatility process can be adjusted to the initial forward variance curve. For this model, excluding trivial cases, we prove that the price process is a true martingale if and only if the truncation order is odd and a sign condition involving the correlation parameter holds.

translated_title: EFM签名波动率模型中的鞅性
translated_abstract: 我们为指数衰减记忆（EFM）签名波动率模型建立了一个鞅性判据，扩展了Abi Jaber、Gassiat和Sotnikov（2026）的近期结果。在所提出的框架中，波动率过程由时间增广布朗运动的EFM签名的线性泛函给出，由此产生一个全局性质良好、完全非马尔可夫且具有平稳分布的波动率模型。通过允许签名取随机初始值，平稳的EFM签名波动率模型也被涵盖在内。此外，波动率过程可以调整以匹配初始远期方差曲线。对于该模型，在排除平凡情形的条件下，我们证明价格过程是真鞅当且仅当截断阶数为奇数且涉及相关性参数的符号条件成立。
tldr: 本文为EFM签名波动率模型建立了鞅性判据，证明在非平凡情形下价格过程是真鞅当且仅当截断阶数为奇数且相关性参数满足特定符号条件。
